metadata.title: Elon Musk’s Boring Company raises $3B at $23B valuation

content.text:
Yahoo Finance Senior Autos Reporter Pras Subramanian joins Market Domination to discuss Elon Musk's tunnel-digging startup, The Boring Company, which announced it raised $3 billion in a Series D funding round, valuing the company at $23 billion
The Boring company that is getting us a a fresh injection of capital investment. So, what's the latest there?
Yeah, you know, you talk about SpaceX a lot, Tesla a lot, everything else, but then Boring still there, right? lying around, boring out tunnels for for, you know, traffic the patterns and things like that. And uh they raised $3 billion in a new series D, uh led by uh interestingly the UAE and various other companies there uh that are related to them, but also like a who's who of PE and VC companies, Human Capital, uh Valor Equity Partners, Sequoia, A A16,
Temasek, which I believe is the Malaysian uh I think is the Malaysian uh sovereign wealth fund, Shama Holdings and Baron Capital. So, uh a lot of big money there for for boring company to sort of uh expand their offerings. They're kind of right now they're currently in Vegas and they're trying to do a new project in in Nashville, in Nashville. and I think they want to expand that.
Anything but boring really when you think about it. And tell us a little bit about Prufrock platform. Uh how critical is the deve- development of that and what is it exactly?
So this is news to me. I guess it's a system where they can sort of
dig and uh collect the material and pull it all out sort of in a more streamlined fashion so you can kind of build faster. Uh and it's that's supposed to make it cheaper to build these and these things are gigantic tunnels, right? You can imagine how much time it takes to build, put in they call them rings to support all the the weight of of the of the earth. So they're doing that. Uh they talk about this thing called uh Z pit, which is Zero people in pit or an autonomous
uh digging uh system and they're they've been debuting that. They did something with a test in August that went pretty well. So I think that's the new future of these pit building or boring or whatever you want to call it.
Wow, that's and everything's always on the West, uh they should make some of that stuff around here just to it'd be pretty cool to go in one of those.
Well, they say one of the problems is is is regulations, zoning. And you can imagine out east, it's a bit harder to do that.
Yeah. A lot harder. All right. Pras, thanks so much.
